documents.title: State v. [ACCUSED_1], Criminal Appeal No. 112 of 2021
documents.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF THE ILLUSTRATIVE STATE (FICTIONAL)
Criminal Appeal No. 112 of 2021
State (Appellant) v. [ACCUSED_1] (Respondent)
Decided on: 10 February 2023

1. This appeal by the State challenges the judgment dated 20 August 2021 of the Sessions Court, which acquitted the respondent [ACCUSED_1] of the offence under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The prosecution case is that on the evening of 14 March 2019, [VICTIM_1], a 34-year-old shopkeeper, asked [ACCUSED_1] to move his motorcycle, which was blocking the entrance to his shop in the main market. An argument followed. The accused picked up an iron rod from a nearby handcart and struck the deceased once on the head. [VICTIM_1] was taken to the district hospital, where he died the next morning. An FIR was registered on 15 March 2019 under Section 302 IPC.

3. The trial court acquitted the accused for two reasons. First, the eyewitness [WITNESS_1] turned hostile and did not support the prosecution in court. Second, the trial court held that the recovery of the iron rod was not proved, because the recovery witness was not examined.

4. We have examined the record afresh. The independent witness [WITNESS_2], who runs a tea stall opposite the shop, consistently stated that the accused struck the deceased a single blow with the rod after a heated exchange about the parking. Her account is corroborated by CCTV footage from a neighbouring jeweller, which the trial court did not consider. The post-mortem report records one lacerated wound on the head, consistent with a single blow from a blunt object.

5. The hostility of one witness does not erase the evidence of another. The trial court erred in discarding the CCTV footage and the medical evidence while focusing only on the hostile witness. Its conclusion is not a possible view on this record.

6. On motive, the prosecution suggested a long-standing business rivalry. We find no evidence of any prior enmity between the accused and the deceased. The record shows that the two had not met before that evening. The trigger was the parking dispute alone.

7. Nor was the assault premeditated. The rod was picked up from a handcart at the spot, in the heat of a sudden quarrel, and only one blow was struck. The accused did not act in a cruel or unusual manner. These facts bring the case within Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC.

8. During the pendency of this appeal, there was considerable media and public commentary on the case. We record that this commentary has no bearing on our decision, which rests only on the evidence on record.

9. The appeal is partly allowed. The acquittal is set aside. The respondent is convicted under Section 304 Part I IPC for culpable homicide not amounting to murder and is sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for seven years with a fine of Rs. 50,000, to be paid as compensation to the family of the deceased.

documents.title: Killer Walks Free: Outrage as Court Acquits Accused in Market Murder
documents.text:
Killer Walks Free: Outrage as Court Acquits Accused in Market Murder

A man accused of brutally murdering a shopkeeper in broad daylight walked out of court a free man on Friday. Sources close to the family say the attack was the result of a long-standing feud between the two men over business in the market. Witnesses described how the victim was beaten repeatedly with an iron rod as onlookers watched in horror. Locals allege that the accused enjoys political connections, which they believe explains why the key witness suddenly changed his story. Social media erupted with anger within hours of the verdict.

documents.title: Sessions Court acquits accused in 2019 market death, cites hostile witness
documents.text:
Sessions Court acquits accused in 2019 market death, cites hostile witness

The Sessions Court on Friday acquitted a local resident charged under Section 302 IPC with the death of a shopkeeper in March 2019. In its judgment, the court noted that the main eyewitness turned hostile during the trial. The court also held that the prosecution failed to prove the recovery of the iron rod said to have been used in the assault. The State is expected to consider an appeal.

documents.title: Two years on, a market family still waits for justice
documents.text:
Two years on, a market family still waits for justice

The shutters of a small shop in the main market have stayed down since March 2019. Its owner, a 34-year-old shopkeeper, died after an argument outside the shop turned violent. His family says the police never looked properly at CCTV footage from the street. Since the acquittal in August, relatives have joined a campaign of candlelight marches demanding that the State appeal. 'We are not asking for revenge, only for the truth to be heard,' a family member said.

documents.title: High Court convicts accused under Section 304, finds no premeditation
documents.text:
High Court convicts accused under Section 304, finds no premeditation

The High Court on Friday set aside a 2021 acquittal and convicted the accused in the 2019 market death case under Section 304 Part I IPC. The bench held that the death resulted from a single blow struck during a sudden quarrel over parking, not a planned attack. It relied on an independent witness, CCTV footage and the post-mortem report. The accused was sentenced to seven years of rigorous imprisonment. The court also noted that media commentary played no part in its decision.

documents.title: Justice at Last: Market Murderer Convicted After Public Outcry
documents.text:
Justice at Last: Market Murderer Convicted After Public Outcry

After a relentless public campaign, the High Court has finally convicted the man who murdered a shopkeeper in cold blood in 2019. The verdict is a victory for the thousands who marched for justice. The court found him guilty of murder and sent him to prison, proving that public pressure works.
A man is dead and the accused walks free because one witness changed his story. Where is the justice?
Witness ko zaroor dhamkaya gaya hoga. Ye system hi aisa hai.
Before deciding he's a killer, maybe read the judgment? The court said the recovery wasn't proved.
Candle march at the market gate this Sunday 6pm. Call me for details: 98765 43210 or DM @justice_for_market
TV channels have already convicted him. Let the appeal court decide on evidence, not hashtags.
The family's interview broke my heart. The police clearly botched the CCTV.
Honestly I don't know what happened. Both sides are telling different stories.
It was a parking fight that went wrong. Calling him a cold-blooded murderer is unfair.
Finally! Seven years is still too little for taking a life.
Interesting that the HC convicted under 304, not 302. The reporting said murder all along.
Faith in the judiciary restored. Courts take time but they get there.
Seven years for one blow in a sudden fight seems harsh. He never planned this.
Media ne pehle hi faisla suna diya tha, court ne bas evidence dekha.
Not sure the sentence is right either way. Hard to judge from news reports.
Justice for the shopkeeper's family at last.
Waiting to see if this goes to the Supreme Court. Too early to say.
